validity.recommendation: no structural change; ref-fill Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Diameter/FuelSource/Location/Owner with the sources below; not a duplicate of any other row in the 35-row roster
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE/ATTRIBUTION all confirmed via multiple independent, GEM-independent origins -- this is one of the best-documented pipelines in the roster. (1) Wikipedia's 'East West Gas Pipeline (India)' article (verified) gives an infobox + prose account: Kakinada (AP) to Bharuch (Gujarat), 48in/1,219.2mm diameter, owner India Infrastructure Trust, current gas source KG-D6 block in the Krishna Godavari Basin, common-carrier authorized. (2) PNGRB's current (31-May-2026) monthly NGPL register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf; large multi-column PDF, url_verifier false-negatives per the documented pattern -- confirmed locally with `pdftotext -layout`) lists row 5 of the OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER table: 'Kakinada-Hyderabad-Uran-Ahmedabad (East West Pipeline)', entity PIL, authorised 21.06.2019, authorised length 1,459 km, authorised+design capacity 85.0 MMSCMD, gas supplied 39.4 MMSCMD (46% utilisation), operating length 1,485 km, states AP/GJ/MH/TS/KA -- independently confirms the pipeline is real, currently operating, common-carrier (=transmission), Gas, and traverses Andhra Pradesh through to Gujarat. (3) The pipeline's operator, Pipeline Infrastructure Limited (PIL), has its own corporate site (pipelineinfra.com) which I read directly and manually confirmed states '...owns and operates a 48 inch diameter pipeline from Kakinada (AP) in the East to Bharuch (Gujarat) in the West with an overall Pipeline Network of 1485 km, including spur and dedicated pipeline' and 'an initial evacuation capacity of approximately 85 MMSCMD' -- exact agreement with GEM's Diameter (48in) and Capacity (85.00 MMSCMD). NOTE: pipelineinfra.com could not be machine-verified by url_verifier -- Python's requests/urllib3 rejects the server's TLS config with 'SSL: UNSAFE_LEGACY_RENEGOTIATION_DISABLED', while `curl` (and presumably any browser) connects fine with 'SSL certificate verify ok' -- this is the documented 'SSL cert-chain errors... confirm via curl' false-negative class in url_verifier.py's own docstring. I could not obtain a passing Wayback snapshot either (archive.org's availability API returned HTTP 429 rate-limit on every retry during this session). Because it never returned an OK from the verifier I have NOT included pipelineinfra.com URLs in any proposed_refs list, but the manual reading is recorded here for a human to re-attempt verification later (e.g. from a different network, or once the Wayback rate-limit clears) -- do not delete this as an unverifiable ref, it is a live, reachable, on-topic corporate source, just one the verifier tool itself cannot currently reach. (4) Gulf Interstate Engineering (the EPCM contractor), via a Wayback-archived case-study page (verified OK), independently corroborates: RIL project, '48-inch diameter natural gas pipeline', 'almost 1,400 kilometers', 'Constructed from 2006 through 2008'. (5) Livemint (verified OK, Sep 2019) independently corroborates OWNERSHIP: 'Brookfield's India Infrastructure Trust, an InvIT, bought RIL's loss-making entity East-West Pipeline for Rs 13,000 crore [in March 2019]. The InvIT took 100% stake in Pipeline Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd that owns and operates the East-West Pipeline' -- matches GEM's Owner1=India Infrastructure Trust 100% exactly, and reconciles with PNGRB's regulatory entity name 'PIL' (the operating subsidiary the Trust wholly owns). CLASSIFICATION: unambiguously a large-diameter (48in), long-haul (>1000km), common-carrier natural-gas trunk line -- correctly 'transmission', not a gathering/feeder/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 35-row India roster -- no other row shares this route (Kakinada AP -> Bharuch GJ); not a relabel or segment double-count of any sibling. Two caveats are broken out as separate concern entries below (LengthKnown and StartYear1) rather than buried here.

validity.recommendation: flag for Update: decide whether LengthKnown=1375 should stay as the original trunk-only figure or be updated to the current total-network figure; do not silently keep 1375 without noting which reading it is
validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH is genuinely ambiguous across sources, and the two readings differ by ~8-10%, which is material. GEM/current sheet: LengthKnown=1375.00 km. Sources supporting ~1375-1400 (an ORIGINAL-TRUNK reading, at commissioning): Wikipedia's own body text states 'EWPL is a...pipeline across the entire trunk length of around 1375 km' (exact match to GEM, though Wikipedia's own infobox on the SAME page instead gives 1,386 km -- the two disagree with each other by 11 km, evidently different vintages of Wikipedia's own editing); Gulf Interstate Engineering's contractor case study (verified) rounds to 'almost 1,400 kilometers'. Sources supporting ~1459-1485 (a CURRENT-TOTAL-NETWORK reading, including spurs/dedicated lines added since commissioning): PNGRB's 31-May-2026 register gives authorised length 1,459 km and operating length 1,485 km for this exact pipeline (row 5, OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER table; confirmed via pdftotext, url_verifier false-negative as documented above); the operator PIL's own corporate site (manually confirmed, not machine-verifiable per the SSL note above) explicitly says 'an overall Pipeline Network of 1485 km, INCLUDING SPUR AND DEDICATED PIPELINE' -- i.e. PIL itself frames 1485 as the full network with branches, distinct from the core 48in trunk. This is consistent with the country-scope guidance's point that PNGRB/operator figures can legitimately exceed an originally-recorded trunk length as a network is built out with spurs over 15+ years of operation (commissioned 2008-2009; PNGRB authorisation itself is dated 21.06.2019, i.e. re-authorised/expanded well after initial commissioning). I am NOT proposing a replacement number since the current GEM value (1375) IS explicitly supported as a valid 'trunk length' reading by Wikipedia's own prose, and correcting to 1485 would be substituting a different SCOPE (total network incl. spurs) for what GEM appears to be recording (the mainline trunk) -- exactly the kind of granularity call the guidance says needs a human decision, not a mechanical overwrite. Flagging as a concern rather than a silent pass so Update makes that call explicitly and, if the total-network reading is preferred, updates LengthKnown with a source note explaining the scope change.

validity.recommendation: flag for Update: StartYear1=2008 vs the operator's own 'commissioning in 2009' -- confirm which convention GEM intends (construction-complete vs first-gas/commercial-commissioning) before treating 2008 as settled
validity.researcher_notes: START YEAR disagreement between sources that both look reasonably authoritative. Sources for 2008 (construction completed): Wikipedia's infobox states 'Commissioned 2008' (citing a now-dead gie.com link) and 'Construction started 2006'; independently, Gulf Interstate Engineering's own Wayback-archived case study (verified OK) -- Gulf was RIL's EPCM contractor on this project, i.e. a first-party engineering account, not a tertiary aggregator -- states 'Constructed from 2006 through 2008'. That is two GEM-independent sources agreeing construction finished in 2008, which is what GEM's StartYear1=2008 currently reflects. However, the CURRENT operator's own corporate website (pipelineinfra.com/operations/, read directly, not machine-verifiable per the SSL false-negative noted in the existence finding above) states plainly: 'Since the commissioning in 2009, PIL has been evacuating Natural Gas from upstream facilities of RIL, ONGC and GSPC on the East Coast...' -- i.e. the entity that actually operates the asset today dates its OWN commissioning to 2009, not 2008. A plausible reconciliation (not confirmed, offered as a lead for Update): RIL's KG-D6 field -- this pipeline's original and named gas source (FuelSource=Krishna Godavari Basin) -- began first gas production in April 2009, so construction/mechanical completion in 2008 and first commercial gas flow ('commissioning' in the operational sense PIL's site uses) in 2009 are both plausible and not mutually exclusive; I could not find a single source that states both dates together to confirm this reconciliation explicitly, so I am not proposing a StartYear2 addition without better evidence. Given a live, current first-party statement from the asset's own operator conflicts with GEM's existing value and its (dead-link-sourced) Wikipedia citation, this is a genuine, material disagreement on a date field and should not be silently passed.
